summary: An interior page of the Jamestown Weekly Alert for September 1886, densely set in six columns across a broadsheet format. The page is an omnibus of local news, civic record, and commercial notices, mixing short City News briefs, county commissioner proceedings, a dissolution notice, Dakota Prize Winners results, a 'Some Quiet Surveying' item, and a substantial block of paid advertising on the right-hand side including the Louisiana State Lottery and Bonds for Sale notices. Editorial tone is matter-of-fact and community-oriented, with no dominant national story; the page reads as a typical interior catch-all for local items that did not make the front page.

clipping_placements.placement_note: set as a brief within the 'From Tuesday's Daily' sub-section of City News, mid-column, between other short docket items

juxtapositions: The Pat Murphy wage-suit digest runs within the same City News column as a notice about the new artesian well machinery arriving in Jamestown, placing a wage dispute between an Irish laborer and a local businessman directly alongside a civic infrastructure story.

The Dissolution Notice for the firm of Kellogg & Tucker sits immediately below the 'At the Front' item about an Anaconda copper-smelting investment opportunity, pairing business failure with business promotion in the same column-foot.
